config.description: read-only PCIe investigation on the secondary GPU server (GA-B250-HD3P-CF, BIOS F8): lspci LnkCap/LnkSta/LnkSta2 + AER on both ends, nvidia-smi link state at idle and under the live 27B workload, sysfs, 128 MiB cuMemcpy x12; initially a single continuous host boot since 2026-11-14. 2026-11-19: three owner-authorized reboots (power-cycle experiments, overriding the original read-only constraint) plus a sysinit-time pre-driver lspci capture. No register writes, no resets, no rebinds.

workload.fixture: 128MiB cuMemcpy; nvidia-smi under the live 27B endpoint load

metrics.name: chipset_card_negotiated_width
metrics.definition: RTX 3060 (EVGA PX1) on the chipset PCIEX4_1 slot (PCH port 00:1d.0, LnkCap x4): negotiated Gen3 x1, measured 2026-11-18 at idle and under load. Historical width across the single continuous boot since 2026-11-14 is unverified (a link can retrain without a reboot); probably x1. The same port verified Gen3 x4 on 2026-08-17/09-06 with the previous card (GTX 1050, via ribbon riser) in it.

metrics.name: chipset_card_h2d_gbps
metrics.definition: median of 12 128 MiB cuMemcpy host-to-device (x1 Gen3 ceiling)

metrics.name: cpu_slot_card_negotiated_width
metrics.definition: RTX 3060 LHR on the CPU x16 slot: Gen3 x16; 8.446/8.110 GB/s H2D/D2H

metrics.name: gtx1050_negotiated_width
metrics.definition: moved to an x1 slot (PCH 00:1c.6, DMI J8B4, LnkCap x1) during the 2026-11-14 installation; Gen3 x1 = slot-limited, not degraded (it did x4 in PCIEX4_1 in Aug/Sep)

metrics.name: gt1030_negotiated_width
metrics.definition: on the second chipset x4 slot (00:1b.0), unchanged since August

metrics.name: aer_errors
metrics.definition: corrected and uncorrected AER counters clean on the chipset card; a stable x1 link can train without errors, so this does not prove the link intended x4

notes: Owner installation knowledge (2026-11-18): the ribbon-riser card sits in PCIEX1_1, next to the CPU; the manual says PCIEX1_1 does not share lanes with PCIEX4_1, so the x1 is not by design. 2026-11-19 (reboot experiment, owner-authorized): the physical layer trains Gen3 at full width on every cold boot (pre-driver capture, 3/3 boots); the NVIDIA driver's post-init path de-trains both links to Gen1 within ~2 minutes of boot, silently (no kernel PCIe events), reproducibly. The chipset card's x1 was an in-epoch width degradation; cold boots negotiate x4. The 2026-11-19 evening review downgraded that reclassification to a HYPOTHESIS: every observation is quiescent and NVIDIA link management reduces generation while idle, so the post-load/post-boot Gen1 state is consistent with idle power management and is not an established defect; whether it persists under sustained traffic is unmeasured. The physical check is now the PRIMARY remaining open question (no longer secondary). The 0.746/0.752 GB/s cuMemcpy figures are Gen3 x1-era measurements (2026-11-18 21:5x) and do not describe the current Gen1 x1/x4 state. Discriminator (planned, no reboot, no kernel parameters): sample generation + width + GPU utilization + PCIe transfer during sustained prefill vs idle. The pcie_aspm=off proposal is withdrawn (NO-GO per review); the remaining open item is the on-site physical check, driver version, BIOS PCIe settings.
